message.nullspace.battery_dead: The battery is dead. It looked just like the others.
message.nullspace.fell: You are not where you were.
message.nullspace.damp_soft: The carpet feels soft. Too soft.
tooltip.nullspace.thermos: Still warm. Restores your grip on reality.
tooltip.nullspace.chalk: Use on a wall to leave a mark
message.nullspace.generator_empty: The generator is silent. Batteries, redstone or coal.
message.nullspace.stability_70: You feel like you're being watched.
message.nullspace.stability_45: You see things that aren't there.
message.nullspace.stadium_leave: The corridor looks different. Or not.
note.nullspace.0.p1:
Day 1. Fell through while digging a mine. Smells of wet carpet and dust. The lamps hum so hard my teeth ache.

Walking along the wall, left hand on it. That's how you get out of mazes.
note.nullspace.0.p2:
Day 4.

The left hand rule doesn't work. The wall ended where there was no wall.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.1.p1:
Don't trust the footsteps behind the wall. They walk when you walk. Stop, and they stop.

I tested it for forty minutes. On the forty-first they didn't stop.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.2.p1:
Every other battery in the crates is dead. I no longer think it's an accident.

Someone puts them there. Someone who wants you to hope.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.3.p1:
Generators work. The old lamps around them light up again, and breathing gets easier.

I slept next to one for six hours. I didn't dream. Best thing that happened to me here.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.4.p1:
Sit in the dark long enough and you start seeing a man.

He stands far away and watches. He has my face.

He vanishes if you look straight at him. I'm not sure he leaves.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.5.p1:
Saw a door. Ordinary, wooden, with a number plate. Shorter than me.

Behind it, a stadium. Empty stands, the scoreboard reads 0:0. The light comes from nowhere.
note.nullspace.5.p2:
I went back out through the same door.

The corridor was different. Or I was.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.6.p1:
I mark the walls with chalk. A cross means I was here.

Today I found an arrow next to my cross.

I don't draw arrows.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.7.p1:
%1$s, if you're reading this — don't sit on the wet stains. The floor is thin there.

I know you'll sit anyway.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.8.p1:
Date: %2$s.

It's my handwriting. I haven't written this yet.
note.nullspace.8.p2:
If you found this note, I guess I'll write it after all.

%1$s, follow the green light. The EXIT sign doesn't lie.

Almost.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.9.p1:
Silence is the worst. When the hum stops you can hear your own heart.

Then you can hear someone else's.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.10.p1:
The tea from the thermos helps. I don't know how.

Maybe it's just warm, and nothing here is warm.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.11.p1:
No windows here. No clocks. No light switches.

Someone else turned the lamps on.

— %1$s
message.nullspace.fell_level1: The floor gives way. Below — water.
message.nullspace.drain: Cold air rises through the grate. Far below, an engine starts.
note.nullspace.12.p1: The level below is pools. The water is murky, like milk mixed with ash. Underwater you can't see your own hands.
note.nullspace.12.p2:
I sat on the edge for an hour. The whole time it felt like something was swimming beside me, just under the surface.

I know there's no one there. I dove. I checked.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.13.p1:
Don't swim for long. Underwater you can't even see your own hands, and after a minute you lose track of which way is up.

Surface sooner than you think you need to.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.14.p1:
At the bottom of the deepest pool there's a drain. The grate is cold and there's a draft.

From below you can hear cars starting. Many cars. None of them go anywhere.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.15.p1:
When the lights go out, everything gets quieter. Even the hum. Even your heart.

I stood in the dark and waited for someone to come. No one came.

No one ever comes.
note.nullspace.15.p2:
Save batteries for the dark. The flashlight is the only thing here that's definitely real.

Well, besides me. Probably.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.16.p1:
The lights die in a wave. First the far ones, then closer, closer, closer.

The last one dies above your head. Then count to twenty. If you make it, the light comes back.

— %1$s
note.nullspace.17.p1:
There's no one here. I checked.

The steps behind the wall are mine. The double is me. The notes are in my handwriting. The chalk arrows are mine too, I just don't remember.

Then why does it always feel like I'm being watched?

— %1$s
